ownershipVerification.evidence: A fresh Symbol is created in execute; module-wide WeakMap associates a client with that token. No shared actor or command state is introduced.

ownershipVerification.evidence: The acquire callback rejects reserved.has(client) before assigning connection. Rejected invocation has no owned connection to query or finalize.

ownershipVerification.evidence: Rollback, close and final cleanup require token equality; rejected callbacks never reach those operations on the foreign client.
check(!reserved.has(client)) and reserved.set(client, owner) are adjacent synchronous statements, with no await or other asynchronous yield.
The same claim check precedes expired/aborted acquisition disposal. Foreign aliases fail without cleanup; an unowned late arrival is claimed only for bounded discard.
owns(client) guards close; catch rollback and final cleanup also check ownership. A normal claim is assigned inside the acquisition callback so cancellation before outer resumption still finds it.

forget deletes only when its captured owner token still matches. Active ownership persists through cleanup acknowledgement or its bounded failure; delayed callbacks cannot unconditionally remove a later claim.
Discard adds to a module-wide WeakSet synchronously before driver cleanup. There is no delete from quarantine. Failed/timed-out/late cleanup cannot permit later SQL on that object.
The provisional success object is internal; result is assigned only after awaited COMMITTED acknowledgement. Rejected/rolled-back and unknown completion keep distinct failure/certainty outcomes.
